questions.problem:
| **Number of Members ($x$)** | $3$ | $4$ | $4$ | $5$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Number of Cars ($y$)** | $2$ | $2$ | $2$ | $6$ |

In a survey of $4$ families, the number of members in each family was recorded as well as the number of cars owned by that family. The data is shown in the table above.
Compute the covariance of the data sets given that the means are $\overset{―}{x}=4$ and $\overset{―}{y}=3.$
questions.worked_solution:
The (population) covariance of the data sets $x={{x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}}$ and $y={{y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{n}}$ is given by 

$$
\text{Cov}(x,y)=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y}),
$$

where $\overset{―}{x}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}$ and $\overset{―}{y}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{y}_{i}$ are the means of the data sets.

Therefore, the covariance of our data sets is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}(x,y) & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[(3-4)(2-3)+(4-4)(2-3)+(4-4)(2-3)+(5-4)(6-3)] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[(-1)(-1)+(0)(-1)+(0)(-1)+(1)(3)] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[1+0+0+3] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot 4 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
| **Years in the 1st division ($x$)** | $44$ | $38$ | $32$ | $30$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Number of Championships ($y$)** | $4$ | $3$ | $3$ | $6$ |

The table above shows the number of years four English soccer teams have been in the top division and the number of national championships they have won. 
Compute the covariance of the data sets.
questions.worked_solution:
The (population) covariance of the data sets $x={{x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}}$ and $y={{y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{n}}$ is given by 

$$
\text{Cov}(x,y)=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y}),
$$

where $\overset{―}{x}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}$ and $\overset{―}{y}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{y}_{i}$ are the means of the data sets.

First, we need to compute the means:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot (44+38+32+30) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot 144 \\  & =36 \\ \overset{―}{y} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{y}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot (4+3+3+6) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot 16 \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the covariance of our data sets is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}(x,y) & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[(44\,-\,36)(4\,-\,4)+(38\,-\,36)(3\,-\,4)+(32\,-\,36)(3\,-\,4)+(30\,-\,36)(6\,-\,4)] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[(8)(0)+(2)(-1)+(-4)(-1)+(-6)(2)] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[0+(-2)+4+(-12)] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot (-10) \\  & =-2.5.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the following data sets:

$$
x={6,\,4,\,8,\,6},\,y={4,\,7,\,11,\,14}
$$

You're given that $\overset{―}{x}=6$ and $\overset{―}{y}=9.$ Calculate $\text{Cov}(x,y).$
questions.worked_solution:
The (population) covariance of the data sets $x={{x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}}$ and $y={{y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{n}}$ is given by 

$$
\text{Cov}(x,y)=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y}),
$$

where $\overset{―}{x}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}$ and $\overset{―}{y}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{y}_{i}$ are the means of the data sets.

Therefore, the covariance of our data sets is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}(x,y) & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[(6-6)(4-9)+(4-6)(7-9)+(8-6)(11-9)+(6-6)(14-9)] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[(0)(-5)+(-2)(-2)+(2)(2)+(0)(5)] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[0+4+4+0] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot 8 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}

questions.problem:
Calculate $\text{Cov}(x,y)$ for the following data sets:

$$
x={-12,\,-10,\,-9,\,-13},\,y={-2,\,0,\,3,\,3}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The (population) covariance of the data sets $x={{x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}}$ and $y={{y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{n}}$ is given by 

$$
\text{Cov}(x,y)=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y}),
$$

where $\overset{―}{x}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}$ and $\overset{―}{y}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{y}_{i}$ are the means of the data sets.

First, we need to compute the means:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot (-12-10-9-13) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot (-44) \\  & =-11 \\ \overset{―}{y} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{y}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot (-2+0+3+3) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot 4 \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the covariance of our data sets is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}(x,y) & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[(-12-(-11))(-2-1)+(-10-(-11))(0-1) \\  & \,\,\,+(-9-(-11))(3-1)+(-13-(-11))(3-1)] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[(-1)(-3)+(1)(-1)+(2)(2)+(-2)(2)] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[3-1+4-4] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot 2 \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
